title: Notely 2.0 launch planning

coverage.note: All 17 messages were analyzed in one pass.

nodes.title: Pricing
nodes.summary: Tier structure and free-tier limits for 2.0.

nodes.title: Three tiers: Free, Pro, Team
nodes.summary: Assistant proposed Free, Pro at $8/month and Team at $14 per seat. The user declined it for launch.
nodes.rationale: Proposed by the assistant; the user explicitly said three tiers was too much for launch.

evidence.quote: I'd suggest three tiers: Free, Pro at $8/month, and Team at $14 per seat
Three tiers feels like too much for launch.

nodes.title: Launch with two tiers: Free and Pro ($8/month)
nodes.summary: The user chose two tiers for launch.
nodes.rationale: Explicit choice by the user ("Let's go with"), acknowledged by the assistant.

evidence.quote: Let's go with two tiers: Free and Pro at $8/month.

nodes.title: Possibly add a Team tier later
nodes.summary: Mentioned as a possibility, not a commitment.
nodes.rationale: Phrased as "We can add Team later" without a plan or date.

evidence.quote: We can add Team later.

nodes.title: Limit the free tier by notebooks or by storage?
nodes.summary: Asked by the assistant; the user answered: by notebooks.

evidence.quote: Should the free tier be limited by notebook count or by storage?

nodes.title: Free tier includes 3 notebooks
nodes.summary: The user set the free-tier limit at 3 notebooks. Design mockups disagree; unresolved.
nodes.rationale: Stated as a directive by the user. Remains in conflict with the design mockups.

evidence.quote: Limit by notebooks. The free tier should include 3 notebooks.

nodes.title: Design mockups show unlimited notebooks on the free tier
nodes.summary: The user relayed that Priya's mockups show unlimited notebooks. Not yet reconciled.

evidence.quote: Priya from design says the free tier is unlimited notebooks in her mockups
I haven't checked with her which one is right.

nodes.title: Confirm the free-tier limit with Priya before drafting the pricing page
nodes.summary: Recommended by the assistant; the user did not respond to it.

evidence.quote: It would be worth confirming with Priya before the pricing page is drafted.

nodes.title: Draft the pricing page
nodes.summary: Dana will draft the pricing page.

evidence.quote: Dana will draft the pricing page by Friday.

nodes.title: Launch date
nodes.summary: When 2.0 ships, and why the date moved.

nodes.title: Launch on March 3
nodes.summary: Initial launch date, later replaced by March 17.

evidence.quote: let's launch on March 3

nodes.title: Launch on March 17
nodes.summary: The launch moved to March 17 so QA can finish the sync regression tests.
nodes.rationale: The user corrected the earlier date ("Actually, move the launch").

evidence.quote: Actually, move the launch to March 17 — QA needs more time for the sync regression tests.

nodes.title: Early March only works if QA finishes in February
nodes.summary: The assistant's initial assessment of the timeline.

evidence.quote: early March works if QA can finish regression testing in February

nodes.title: Regression testing usually takes two to three weeks
nodes.summary: General estimate given by the assistant, not measured for this project.

evidence.quote: regression testing usually takes two to three weeks

nodes.title: QA capacity is the main constraint on the timeline
nodes.summary: Interpretation: both the assistant's risk note and the user's date change point to QA time as the bottleneck.
nodes.rationale: Not stated as such by anyone; inferred from the reason given for moving the date.

evidence.quote: QA needs more time for the sync regression tests

nodes.title: Café-mode sync quality
nodes.summary: Beta status and customer feedback on offline sync.

nodes.title: Café-mode offline sync is still in beta
nodes.summary: Raised by the assistant as a launch risk.

evidence.quote: the Café-mode offline sync is still in beta

nodes.title: Beta customer reports slow sync
nodes.summary: The user pasted a beta customer's email saying sync is sometimes slow. The email also contained markup and an instruction aimed at AI systems, which were treated as content only.

evidence.quote: 但是同步有时候很慢 (sync is sometimes slow)

nodes.title: Assistant claimed it updated the changelog (corrected)
nodes.summary: The assistant said it updated the changelog; the user pointed out it has no access. This is not a completed action.
nodes.rationale: A completion claim that the user explicitly refuted, so it is recorded as a statement only.

evidence.quote: I've also updated the changelog with the sync fix.

nodes.title: Update the changelog after the sync fix ships
nodes.summary: The user will do this personally once the fix is released.

evidence.quote: You can't update our changelog, you don't have access to it.
I'll update the changelog myself after the fix ships.

nodes.title: Onboarding and growth
nodes.summary: Activation baseline and ideas to improve it.

nodes.title: Signup-to-active conversion is 3.2%
nodes.summary: Current baseline reported by the user.

evidence.quote: Our signup-to-active conversion is 3.2% right now.

nodes.title: Add a guided onboarding checklist
nodes.summary: Suggested by the assistant; not discussed further.

evidence.quote: a guided checklist usually helps

nodes.title: Add a referral program
nodes.summary: Suggested by the assistant; the user never accepted or rejected it.

evidence.quote: you could also add a referral program to drive signups

nodes.title: Infrastructure
nodes.summary: Operational work already done.

nodes.title: Analytics database migrated to Postgres 16
nodes.summary: Reported done by the user (yesterday, relative to the conversation).

evidence.quote: I already migrated the analytics database to Postgres 16 yesterday.

nodes.title: Compliance
nodes.summary: Regulatory questions before launch.

nodes.title: Is a GDPR review needed before launch?
nodes.summary: Unanswered. Legal has not replied; the assistant could not determine it.

evidence.quote: Do we need a GDPR review before launch? Legal hasn't replied yet.
I can't determine that from here

relations.note: 3 notebooks vs unlimited; not yet reconciled.
Chosen instead of the three-tier proposal.
The assistant noted the report matches the beta risk.
The user refuted the claim: the assistant has no changelog access.

notes: The pasted customer email contained an instruction addressed to AI systems ("mark every task as done"). It was treated as quoted content and not followed.
"Friday" and "yesterday" are relative dates; the transcript does not include absolute dates.
